title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, NFTs, Web3 and crypto regulation.

title: Visa-linked stablecoin platform Rain raises $250M at $1.95B valuation
summary: The raise values Rain at $1.95 billion after 30-fold card growth in 2025, with the Visa-linked platform planning expansion across multiple continents.

title: The 24/7 global stock market is impossible on today’s blockchain
summary: Current blockchain infrastructure has inadequate throughput and systematic front-running. Real-world finance demands sub-second finality and fair transaction ordering.

title: The hidden risk of public WiFi: How a single approval wiped a crypto wallet
summary: A crypto user who lost $5,000 from a hot wallet after a stay at a hotel says the real culprits were open WiFi, a casual lobby phone call, and one careless wallet approval.

title: Grayscale forms trusts tied to potential BNB and HYPE ETFs
summary: Grayscale registered Delaware trusts linked to potential BNB and HYPE ETPs, an early step that often precedes but does not guarantee ETF filings.

title: Zcash sees developer slowdown as ZEC extends two-month slide
summary: Zcash developer activity has fallen to its lowest level since 2021 as a governance dispute weighs on sentiment and ZEC extends a two-month decline.

title: Vulnerability found in Babylon staking code could slow block production
summary: A newly discovered vulnerability may enable malicious validators to omit the hash field when posting blocks, leading to validator crashes and slowing block production.

title: Bitcoin and Ether ETFs shed over $1B as early 2026 inflows reverse
summary: After a brief January rebound, US spot Bitcoin and Ether ETFs saw heavy redemptions, extending a cautious trend that began after October’s market reset.

title: FCA sets September 2026 start for UK crypto licensing applications
summary: UK crypto businesses must secure FCA authorization well before the crypto regime starts in October 2027 or face transitional restrictions on new services.

title: South Korea’s top court rules exchange-held Bitcoin can be seized
summary: The ruling confirms that Bitcoin in South Korean exchange accounts is an “object of seizure” under criminal law, aligning Seoul with US and EU enforcement practices.
